facts.text: After Aldrich's death, his monstrous form dissolved, revealing Gwyndolin's remains had finally stopped moving inside him.
Among Aldrich's remains lay a cleric's staff, hinting at his origins before becoming a monster.
The cinders of a lord found within Aldrich's remains proved he had once linked the first flame.
The Ashen One found a sword belonging to Anri of Astora among the ruins near Aldrich, suggesting Anri had tried to confront Aldrich before the Ashen One arrived.
After defeating Aldrich, two Lords of Cinder (the Abyss Watchers and Aldrich) had been put to rest, leaving Yhorm the Giant and Prince Lothric unaccounted for.
The Irithyll Dungeon is a network of cells and torture chambers beneath Irithyll where Pontiff Sulyvahn's regime imprisoned and disposed of threats to its authority.
The Profaned Capital is a ruined city covered in ash, with streets sunk into poisonous swamps, once ruled by Yhorm the Giant.
Yhorm the Giant was descended from an ancient conqueror whose lineage predated the current crisis by generations.
Yhorm the Giant ruled over a population of humans in the Profaned Capital and tried to protect and stabilize them despite his massive size compared to them.
A curse combined with the interference of unscrupulous court sorcerers caused the eruption of the Profaned Flame in Yhorm's capital.
The Profaned Flame could not be extinguished, burned without fuel, and seemed to actively seek out human life.
The Profaned Flame destroyed every human being in the Profaned Capital, while Yhorm the Giant survived because giants were hardier than humans.
In grief over his people's destruction, Yhorm the Giant chose to link the first flame, hoping his sacrifice would subdue the Profaned Flame.
Yhorm the Giant possessed two identical Storm Ruler greatswords capable of channeling the power of storms.
Before linking the flame, Yhorm the Giant gave one Storm Ruler to his trusted friend, Siegward of Catarina, with instructions to use it against him if he ever returned as a threat.
Yhorm the Giant became a Lord of Cinder by linking the first flame, but the Profaned Flame continued to rain down and devastate his capital regardless.
When the Lords of Cinder were resurrected by the tolling of the emergency bell, Yhorm the Giant returned to find his capital unchanged, still in ruins.
Yhorm the Giant retreated to his throne room, sitting with his great machete across his knees, waiting without purpose.
When the Ashen One confronted Yhorm the Giant, a Storm Ruler greatsword lay near his throne, possibly placed deliberately by Yhorm himself.
The Storm Ruler greatsword can unleash gusts of thunderous wind capable of staggering Yhorm the Giant, who is otherwise resistant to conventional weapons.
In some versions of the fight, Siegward of Catarina arrives to help the Ashen One defeat Yhorm the Giant, honoring his old promise.
The Ashen One defeated Yhorm the Giant and claimed his cinders of a lord, marking the third Lord of Cinder dealt with.
After three Lords of Cinder (Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, Yhorm) were defeated, only Prince Lothric remained unaccounted for.
High Priestess Emma, dying at the altar in the chapel, delivered her final message to the Ashen One, urging them to make Prince Lothric become a lord and save the world.
High Priestess Emma gave the Ashen One the Basin of Vows, an artifact needed to access Lothric Castle.
High Priestess Emma died immediately after giving the Ashen One the Basin of Vows and her final message.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley, one of Pontiff Sulyvahn's Outrider Knights, appeared in the chapel after Emma's death to stop the Ashen One.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley was, like Vordt, once an Irithyllian Outrider Knight of old royal lineage before being transformed by Sulyvahn's cursed eye rings.
Pontiff Sulyvahn stationed the Dancer of the Boreal Valley and a division of Outriders in Lothric for unclear purposes.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley wields one sword burning with phantom flame and another emanating cold dark mist.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley alternates between slow, elegant attacks and a wild spinning spiral attack that sets the floor ablaze.
The Ashen One defeated the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, who collapsed into black ash.
Placing the Basin of Vows on the altar statue in the chapel activated a hidden mechanism, lowering a ladder up into Lothric Castle.
Lothric Castle is filled with hollowed knights who continue to fight with the discipline they had in life, despite having lost their minds.
Shrieking stone gargoyles that once served as architectural decorations in Lothric Castle have been animated and attack intruders from above.
Two ancient wyverns guard a balcony in Lothric Castle, breathing fire and blocking passage to the upper reaches.
The Ashen One killed one wyvern in Lothric Castle by leaping from higher ground and stabbing it through the skull.
The second wyvern in Lothric Castle was controlled by a parasitic pilgrim insect; killing the insect caused the wyvern to stop moving.
Pilgrim butterflies in Lothric Castle are the corrupted remains of pilgrims who once sought the castle or its archives, now transformed into ghostly floating creatures.
Some knights in Lothric Castle exhibit abyssal growths on their armor, showing that the Abyss's corruption has spread into the castle.
The Dragon Slayer Armor, an ancient relic from the age of dragon-hunting knights, is animated by pilgrim butterflies and guards the bridge to the Grand Archives.
The Dragon Slayer Armor wields a massive great axe and shield, both crackling with lightning.
The Ashen One defeated the Dragon Slayer Armor, causing it to collapse and the controlling pilgrim butterflies to scatter.
The Grand Archives of Lothric house generations of accumulated knowledge, but the books themselves are cursed and attack intruders.
Pools of melted wax in the Grand Archives can be used to coat the head, creating a protective barrier against the cursed spirits inhabiting the books.
Cursed wax scholars, former researchers of the Grand Archives, now attack intruders rather than pursue knowledge.
Living bookshelves in the Grand Archives detach from walls and attack intruders.
A surviving Crystal Sage, the sibling of the one fought in the Cathedral of the Deep's woods, appears in the Grand Archives allied with Lothric.
The Ashen One defeated the surviving Crystal Sage in the Grand Archives.
At the top of the Grand Archives, three elite warriors called the Three Pillars of the king's rule - Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui, and Cream Hild - guard the path to Prince Lothric.
Lion Knight Albert fights with disciplined, precise sword and shield technique in service to the king.
Black Hand Kamui is a royal assassin who fights with twin blades and extreme speed.
Cream Hild is a sorceress who provides magical support with crystal projectiles and energy bolts.
The Ashen One defeated the Three Pillars (Albert, Kamui, and Cream Hild) one at a time on a balcony above the Grand Archives.
After the Three Pillars fell, the Ashen One ascended via lift through a garden and bridge to the highest tower where Prince Lothric and Lorian waited.
Prince Lothric sits on a throne, pale, sickly, and physically weak, but possesses arcane abilities.
Lorian is Prince Lothric's elder brother, once a renowned knight, who knelt before the throne, having lost the use of his legs and voice.
Lorian willingly took on part of Prince Lothric's curse to share his burden, losing his own legs and voice as the price.
An unnamed mentor encouraged Prince Lothric to question the necessity of the endless cycle of sacrifice, fueling his decision to reject the flame.
Lorian supported Prince Lothric's decision to reject the flame and followed him into isolation in the tower.
The emergency bell that resurrected the Lords of Cinder tolled because of Prince Lothric and Lorian's joint refusal to link the flame.
In the final battle, Lorian fights using a flaming greatsword and teleports via bursts of flame despite being unable to walk.
